label.description: The accessible name of the toolbar, and it is not optional in practice: a toolbar is a container a reader is told they have entered, and an unnamed one is announced by its role alone. toolbar is in neither of the accessibility lint's named-role sets, so nothing lints its absence — the element's own test pins it instead, and so does every surface that mounts one.

orientation.description: horizontal or vertical. It chooses which arrow pair moves the caret between controls, and it turns the row through 90 degrees off aria-orientation — which role=toolbar both supports and defaults to horizontal, so unlike jx-action-group there is no second data- attribute to key the layout on.

onKeydown.description: The toolbar keyboard contract: the arrow pair of its own axis moves the roving caret between reachable controls with wrap, Home and End go to the ends, and a control that answers the key itself keeps it — a text field holds the arrows while its caret has text left to walk in that direction, and holds Home and End always.

onReady.description: Collapses the toolbar to one tab stop once it has rendered, and keeps it collapsed to one as controls come and go. It listens for the element's own jx-ready because onMount is handed the reactive scope alone, and placing a caret needs the host.

emits.name: jx-ready
emits.description: The toolbar has rendered and distributed its children, so its caret can be placed.

onMount.description: Announces that the element has rendered. The toolbar's own onReady listens for it, and a host may too.
